# `Q-15-2` — Duplicate Crossref Identifier Across Chapters

> A crossref identifier (such as a `fig-`/`tbl-` label or an
> explicit `#id`) is defined in more than one chapter of the same
> book.

## What this means

In a multi-file book, every chapter's cross-reference targets share
one project-wide namespace: a reference like `@fig-plot` written in
*any* chapter must resolve to exactly one element in the whole book.
Each crossref id must therefore be **unique across all chapters**,
not just within the chapter that defines it.

This error fires when two different chapters define the same id —
for example, both `chapter1.qmd` and `chapter3.qmd` contain a figure
labeled `#| label: fig-plot`. The diagnostic underlines **both**
occurrences (the first definition and the duplicate) and names the
chapters involved.

Quarto keeps the **first** chapter's definition (in book chapter
order) and ignores the duplicate, so the render still completes —
but references to that id resolve to the first chapter's target,
which may not be the one you meant.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **Copy-paste between chapters** — a figure or table block was
  copied into another chapter and its `label:` / `#id` was not
  changed.
- **Parallel structure** — chapters that intentionally mirror each
  other (e.g. one figure per case study) reusing the same labels.
- **A template or include** that carries a labeled element being
  pulled into more than one chapter.

## How to fix

Give one of the targets a different identifier so each is unique
across the book:

- For computational figures/tables, change the `#| label:` option
  in one of the chapters (e.g. `fig-plot` and `fig-plot-survey`).
- For explicit ids, change the `{#fig-plot}` attribute.

Then update any `@`-references that should point at the other
target. If the duplicated element does not need to be
cross-referenceable, removing its label also resolves the error.
